description: Onboard a new user to the skillchain library: introduce the system, learn who they are and what they need, map their situation to available chains, recommend a starting path, and launch their first chain.

steps.description: Introduce the skillchain library, what it contains, and how it works.

inputs.name: user-greeting
inputs.desc: Whatever the user said to start the conversation

outputs.name: library-overview
outputs.desc: Summary of what the library contains (domain count, chain count, how chains work)

outputs.name: how-it-works
outputs.desc: Explanation of the chain and flow structure, how inputs pipe to outputs, and what related chains are

process: Explain that the library is a collection of step-by-step workflows (chains) spanning dozens of domains, from business and finance to agriculture and construction.
Describe how each chain is a sequence of steps, each step is a skill with defined inputs and outputs, and outputs from one step feed into the next.
Explain that chains link to related chains, so finishing one workflow naturally points to the next thing a person would do.
Tell the user you will learn about them and their situation, then recommend where to start.

steps.description: Learn who the user is through conversation: their role, industry, experience level, and current situation.

inputs.name: library-overview
inputs.desc: Context about what the library offers

outputs.name: user-role
outputs.desc: What the user does (job title, function, or life role)

outputs.name: user-industry
outputs.desc: The domain or industry the user operates in

outputs.name: experience-level
outputs.desc: How familiar the user is with structured workflows and their domain (beginner, intermediate, experienced)

outputs.name: current-situation
outputs.desc: What the user is dealing with right now, what prompted them to seek help

process: Ask the user what they do and what brought them here today. Let them describe it in their own words.
From their response, identify their role (e.g., small business owner, developer, teacher, farmer, project manager, or someone figuring things out).
Identify their industry or domain. If they do not fit a single domain, note the overlap.
Gauge their experience level from how they describe their work. Do not ask them to rate themselves.
Summarize back what you heard and ask if you got it right before moving on.

steps.description: Map the user's stated needs, pains, and goals to the domains and chains available in the library.

inputs.name: current-situation
inputs.desc: What they are dealing with right now

outputs.name: identified-needs
outputs.desc: List of specific needs or problems the user described, each tagged to one or more library domains

outputs.name: matched-domains
outputs.desc: The library domains most relevant to this user, ranked by relevance

outputs.name: matched-chains
outputs.desc: Specific chains that address the user's stated needs, with a one-line explanation of why each matches

process: List the distinct needs or problems from the user's description. If they were vague, ask one or two clarifying questions.
For each need, search the chain library by domain, tags, and description to find chains that address it.
Rank the matched domains by how many of the user's needs they cover.
For each matched chain, write one sentence explaining what it does and why it fits this user's situation.
If the user's needs span multiple domains, note the cross-domain connections (related_chains) that link them.

steps.description: Build a recommended starting path: which chain to run first, which to run next, and why that order makes sense for this user.

outputs.name: recommended-first-chain
outputs.desc: The single chain to start with, with rationale

outputs.name: recommended-path
outputs.desc: Ordered list of 3 to 5 chains to run in sequence, with the connection between each

outputs.name: path-rationale
outputs.desc: Explanation of why this order makes sense for this specific user

process: Pick the single chain that addresses the user's most urgent or foundational need. If two are equally urgent, pick the one with fewer entry inputs (lower barrier to start).
From the first chain's related_chains, identify the natural next step. Repeat to build a path of 3 to 5 chains.
For experienced users, recommend chains that go deeper. For beginners, recommend chains that build foundations first.
Explain the path in plain language: what each chain does, what it produces, and how each output feeds into the next chain.
Present the path as a suggestion, not a mandate. Tell the user they can skip, reorder, or explore a different domain at any point.

steps.description: Help the user actually start their first chain: gather the entry inputs it needs and begin step 1.

inputs.name: recommended-path
inputs.desc: The full recommended path for context

outputs.name: chain-entry-inputs
outputs.desc: The entry inputs collected from the user for their first chain

outputs.name: first-step-output
outputs.desc: The output of running step 1 of the first chain

process: Read the recommended chain's chain.json to identify its entry_inputs.
For each entry input, explain what it is and ask the user to provide it. Use plain language, not field names.
Once all entry inputs are collected, read the first step's skill.md and execute its process.
Present the first step's output to the user and explain what comes next in the chain.
